name: TX-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Pfluger running with large financial advantage ($2.9M cash vs $47K)
No public polling or expert ratings; markets price Democrat at ~3%
model.rationale: Pfluger holds a heavily Republican West Texas seat, has raised over $3.1 million against a challenger with under $90,000, and prediction markets give Reynolds about a 3% chance. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though a seat this red is unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-11 is a deeply Republican district in West Texas, with a partisan lean of about R+17. August Pfluger, the incumbent, is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. Claire Reynolds is the Democratic nominee, but the race shows few signs of competitiveness.

The financial picture is lopsided: Pfluger has raised roughly $3.2 million and holds $2.9 million on hand, while Reynolds has raised under $90,000 with less than $50,000 available. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, no public polls cover the race, and prediction markets price Reynolds' chances at only about 3%. Everything points to a safe Republican hold.
